Okay, let's get started, it's just after ten so I think everyone who is joining is here. This is the weekly product sync for the Pathway mobile app. I'm Meera, I'll run the meeting today. We have Arjun from engineering, Sofia from design, Daniel from marketing, and Kavya from customer support. The agenda is the release date for version 2.4, the onboarding redesign, the crash rate on older Android phones, the marketing launch plan, and support staffing. Let's start with the release.

Arjun, where are we with version 2.4? Sure. So the feature work is done. Offline mode is merged, the new search is merged, and the payment retry flow is merged. What is not done is the crash fix for Android 10 devices. Right now the crash-free session rate on Android 10 is ninety-four percent, and our release bar is ninety-nine percent. Everything else is above ninety-nine. So my honest view is that we cannot ship on the twentieth of March as planned if that crash is still there. How long do you think the fix takes? We traced it to the image cache. When the device is low on memory the cache is not released and the app is killed. The fix itself is maybe two days, plus three days of testing on the device lab. So realistically the build would be ready by the twenty-seventh.

Okay. So the options are, we ship on the twentieth without the fix and do a hot fix later, or we move the release to the twenty-seventh. Daniel, what does a one-week slip do to marketing? It is fine as long as we decide today. The press embargo is flexible, the only hard date is the partner webinar on the third of April, and the twenty-seventh still gives us a week before that. Kavya, support view? Please don't ship the crash. Android 10 is about eighteen percent of our active users and those crash tickets are the most painful ones we get. Okay, then I think we're agreed. We are moving the 2.4 release to the twenty-seventh of March, and we will not ship until the Android 10 crash-free rate is above ninety-nine percent. Does anyone disagree? No? Good, that's decided.

Arjun, you own the image cache fix. Can you have the fix merged by Wednesday? Yes, I'll have it merged by Wednesday and the device lab results by Friday. Great. And who signs off on the crash numbers before release? I think it should be QA, but we don't have a QA lead since Rohan left. Okay, let's park that, it's an open question who gives the final quality sign-off. I'll raise it with leadership.

Second topic, onboarding redesign. Sofia, go ahead. So we tested the new onboarding with twelve users last week. The old flow has five screens, the new flow has three screens and lets people skip account creation until they save their first route. In testing, nine out of twelve people finished the new flow without help, compared to six out of twelve on the old flow. The main complaint was that the permission request for location appears too early. People don't understand why we need location before they've seen the app. So my suggestion is to move the location permission prompt to the moment someone first opens the map. Arjun, is that a big change? No, that's small, it's an afternoon of work. Then let's do that. Moving the location prompt to first map open is approved.

Are we shipping the new onboarding in 2.4? I would rather not. It needs another round of testing with the permission change, and I don't want to mix it with the crash fix. Okay so onboarding goes into 2.5, not 2.4. Sofia will run a second round of user testing with the updated flow. Sofia, when can you have that done? I can test with eight users by the end of next week, so the fourteenth. Good.

There was one more thing on onboarding. Should we make account creation mandatory for the premium trial? Daniel thinks yes because of fraud, Sofia thinks no because it hurts conversion. We don't have data on trial fraud yet. Kavya, do you know how many trial abuse cases support has seen? I don't have the number, I'd have to pull it. Okay, so that one stays open. We need the fraud numbers before deciding. Kavya will pull the trial abuse numbers from the support system before the next sync.

Third, marketing launch. Daniel? So with the new date, the plan is: blog post and email to existing users on the release day, the twenty-seventh. App store screenshots need to be updated for offline mode. And we want to do a paid social campaign. The proposed budget for the campaign is fifteen thousand dollars for the first month. Is that approved? I can't approve fifteen thousand on my own, that needs finance. My suggestion is we prepare the campaign but don't commit spend until finance approves. Fine. So the campaign budget is not approved yet, it's pending finance. Daniel, can you send the budget request to finance by Monday? Yes, I'll send it Monday. And the screenshots? Sofia can you do the screenshots? Yes, I'll do the new screenshots by the twenty-fourth so they're ready before release.

One question from my side, Daniel. Are we doing anything for the partner webinar on the third of April? We should, but I don't know who presents. Ideally someone from product. Okay let's leave that open for now, we'll decide who presents at the webinar next week.

Last topic, support staffing. Kavya. So ticket volume went up thirty percent after the last release, mostly about payments. We have two support agents and we're at our limit. I'd like to hire one contractor for six weeks around the 2.4 launch. What does that cost? Around six thousand dollars total. I think that's reasonable given the crash tickets we're trying to avoid. I can approve that one, it's within my budget. So hiring one support contractor for six weeks is approved. Kavya, can you start the hiring? Yes, I'll post the role today and aim to have someone by the twentieth.

Okay, let me recap. Decisions: release 2.4 moves to the twenty-seventh of March, no release until Android 10 crash-free rate is above ninety-nine percent. The location permission prompt moves to first map open. The new onboarding ships in 2.5, not 2.4. One support contractor for six weeks is approved. Action items: Arjun merges the image cache fix by Wednesday and shares device lab results by Friday. Sofia runs the second onboarding test by the fourteenth and updates screenshots by the twenty-fourth. Daniel sends the campaign budget request to finance on Monday. Kavya pulls trial abuse numbers before next sync and posts the contractor role today. Open items: who gives final quality sign-off now that we have no QA lead, whether account creation should be mandatory for the premium trial, whether finance approves the fifteen thousand dollar campaign, and who presents at the partner webinar.
